newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU uncovers more farm fraud in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU uncovers more farm fraud in 1996.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it uncovered slightly more farm fraud in 1996 -- 2,016 cases, mostly in cereals, beef and olive oil, totalling 345 million Ecus.
In 1995, the EU found 1,853 cases worth 319 million Ecus.
"The big fraudsters take advantage of the system of market support and export refunds," it said in an annual report.
Member states reported 124 cases of cereals fraud worth 62.6 million Ecus, 231 cases of beef fraud worth 20.0 million Ecus and 252 cases of olive oil fraud worth 32.1 million Ecus.
Reported farm fraud amounted to only 0.8 percent of EU farm spending of 42.8 billion Ecus in 1996.
Although agricultural market support and export refunds have almost halved since 1992, detected fraud has risen to two percent of spending in the two areas.
Direct payments to farmers have doubled to 57 percent, from 29 percent, of total farm spending over the same period.
In Italy 476 cases amounting to 123.5 million Ecus were reported. Only 1.5 million has been recovered.
In Germany, 479 cases of fraud were reported for a value of 25.5 million Ecus. Britain reported 245 fraud cases for 4.1 million and Spain 122 cases for 16.5 million.
